title: Push width further: ASPECT_RATIO 112 (model_dim=896)
description: Deliberately diverged from the 5/6 identical ASPECT_RATIO=96 proposals to bracket the width optimum from above: ASPECT_RATIO 80->112 (model_dim 640->896, 7 heads) with DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->64 for VRAM safety.
reflection: Clear regression: val_bpb 1.035625, much worse than the 0.999094 baseline (and worse than the pre-width-scaling 1.012413 baseline too). Only 418 optimizer steps completed (fewer tokens seen) vs presumably 500+ at dim=640/batch=128, and peak VRAM was only 38.9GB -- well under ceiling, so this wasn't VRAM-limited, it was undertrained: the model got too big and/or the smaller device batch (more grad-accum steps, same effective batch) traded per-step efficiency for capacity at a bad point on the curve. This confirms the width-scaling gain from 512->640 does NOT extrapolate linearly -- 896 is past the sweet spot for this 5-minute wall-clock budget. Whoever is tracking the group's ASPECT_RATIO=96 (768-dim) runs: if those also come back worse than 640, the true optimum is likely between 640 and 768, not above it. I would NOT recommend anyone spend another slot pushing width past 768 without first confirming 768 itself beats 640.
